Title: S. Thasci Caecili Cypriani Opera Spuria, cum Indicibus et Praefatione (CSEL 3, Pars III); includes the Vita Caecilii Cypriani attributed to Pontius the deacon, and the Acta Proconsularia
Creator: Cyprian of Carthage (spuria, disputed/pseudonymous works); Pontius the Deacon (Vita, traditionally but not certainly attributed); Wilhelm (Guilelmus) Hartel (Editor)
Publisher: Vindobonae (Vienna), Apud C. Geroldi filium bibliopolam Academiae, Corpus Scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum Latinorum (CSEL) vol. 3, Pars III
Publication Date: 1871
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication; archive.org metadata records possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT)
Language: lat
Source: archive.org item corpusscriptorum03cypruoft (contributor: Trinity College, University of Toronto; scanned 2006), full text at https://archive.org/download/corpusscriptorum03cypruoft/corpusscriptorum03cypruoft_djvu.txt. Fetched directly by this build thread 2026-09-08, closing this world's own Source_Acquisition_Manifest G1 request's open Pars III gap. A sibling research session (session_01WLxhNbVhjkf1R2SAh8dxxT, branch claude/latin-pastoral-source-integration) had independently located and vendored closely related material from the same edition; this file was independently re-fetched and re-verified against archive.org directly rather than adopted from that session's own copy.
Provenance note: Mechanically extracted from the item's own djvu.txt. Front-matter scan noise (a Trinity College Toronto library flyleaf stamp) stripped before the title page. The scanned volume is physically bound together with CSEL 4 (Arnobius, Adversus Nationes, ed. Reifferscheid, 1875); that second, unrelated work begins immediately after this file's own end and was cut entirely, not included. Doubled inter-word spacing (an OCR/scan artifact) normalized to single spaces; nothing else altered, no OCR error corrected. Note (independent review, Round 18; extended, Round 20): quotations in this header (Content note, Source line, Title, or this Provenance note itself) are given in standard/readable spelling for legibility; the file's own OCR carries the usual scan-level noise at some of the same points -- letter confusions (V/Y, C/G, u/n and similar), and, at points of heavier degradation, a single word broken into multiple tokens or joined with an adjacent one. A reader matching a quoted phrase against the file directly should expect this range of variation, not a discrepancy in substance; the file's own body text, not this header's quotation of it, is authoritative for exact wording. Public domain by publication date (1871), independently confirmed by archive.org's own rights metadata.
Content note: This file carries three components in sequence: (1) Cyprian's own spuria (works transmitted under his name but not by him), (2) the Vita Caecilii Cypriani attributed to Pontius the deacon (title page: "VITA CAECILII CYPRIANI (Pontio diacono uulgo adscripta)"), and (3) the Acta Proconsularia (Cyprian's own trial and martyrdom record). This is the Latin original standing behind the already-vendored ANF05 English translation of Pontius's Life (Registry row 7). The apparatus criticus is noisier than the running text throughout; the running Latin text itself reads coherently, including at the Vita's own end.

PEAEFATIO.

Duodecim abusiua sunt saeculi. hoc est: sapieus sine operibus,
senex sine religione , adulescens sine oboedientia , diues sine eleemo-
syna, femina sine pudicitia, dominus sine uirtute, christiauus con- s
tentiosus , pauper superbus , rex iniquus , episcopus neglegens , plebs
sine disciplina, populus sine lege. sic suffocatur iustitia: liaec sunt
duodecim abusina saeculi per quae saeculi rota, si in illo fuerint, deci-
pitur et ad tartari tenebras nullo impediente iustitiae suffragio per
iustum Dei iudicium rotatur. lo

PRAEFATIO.

Cum academia litterarum c. Vindobonensis iiouum corpus
scriptorum ecclesiasticorum latinorum qui ad optimorum et
uetustissimorum codicum fidem redigerentur ante hos sex anuos
edere constituisset, Cypriani opera recensendi munus milii ob-
tulit; qua in re eximia eius liberalitate omnibus fere manu-
scriptis libris quorum in lectionum iudicio est aliqua auctoritas
mibi uti licuit, ut si hanc editiouem cum reliquis contuleris
scriptoris uerba inuumeris locis emeudata et ad genuinam for-
mam redacta inuenias. ex bibliothecarum uero scriniis tauta
librorum multitudo quorum non exiguam partem nemo adhuc
inspexerat praesto fuit, ut subsidiorum copia paene laborarem.
nam non ea est horum operum condicio, id quod in profanis
scriptoribus non ita raro occurrit, ut omnes codices ex uno codice
archetypo ducti unius sint stirpis in paucas quasdam familias
diuisae; quo enim frequentius et lectitabantur et describebantur
Cypriani seripta, eo procliuior erat horum emendatio et inter-
polatio eoque plures exstiterunt codicum familiae neque intactam
suorum arehetyporum iutegritatem conseruabant apographa.
deinde non eadem est singulorum operum condicio aut una eius-
dem codicis jter diuersas operum partes auctoritas; cum enim
proptor amplitudincm hoc coii^us particuhitim describeretur,
sua est siugularum partium e diuersis archetypis profectarum
critica ratio, suum subsidiorum instrumentum. bene igitur sin-
gulari quodam casu euenit, ut nonnulli codices uetustissimi
eidemque integerrimi hodie exsteut, quorum auxilio difficilis

alioquin de codicum singulorum praestantia ac cognatione quaestio

sequi. est uero minor operum pars, libelli fere omnes priore

ibi cum duces habeamus, hoc negotio supersedere iam possumus,
ut reliquorum codicum, prout aut conspirant inter se aut dis-
crepant, familias describamus; nam in iis locis, quales pauci
sunt, ubi optimorum testium auxilio destituti ex reliquis codici-
bus uerba constituamus necesse est, nuUus unus codex aut nulla
una codicum famiiia sic prae ceteris excellit, ut in eligendis
scripturis, quarum nulla non per se satis probabilis haberi possit,
ea auctoritate iudicium regatur. epistulae autem cum paucae
tantum in codicibus pari uetustate conmendatis exstent, prius-
quam tententur, codices qui e quibus archetypis per quas uicissi-
tudines ducti sint accurate debent circumspici et ponderari.
progredimur igitur ad primum huius disputationis caput, ut

utendum quaeramus.
